summary: Midday p99 sawtooth from eviction-feedback loop: autoscaler shrink after IO-latency misread & noisy-tenant prefetch storm
description: Issue summary: During the customer's midday traffic window we observed repeating p99 latency spikes in their dedicated pool. The pattern is a sawtooth: latency climbs over ~10 minutes, spikes at p99, then drops after a partial autoscaler shrink and subsequent reattach. Impact: SparrowAI sees intermittent failed transactions and degraded tail latency causing degraded user experience and increased timeouts for a subset of routed traffic. Environment: Dedicated pool (us-west) serving SparrowAI's reserved capacity; autoscaler in predictive+reactive hybrid mode; KV-prefetch enabled; tenant pinned to model variants. Observed behavior: Autoscaler reported low 'active slot' utilization before a shrink, then evictions occur, followed by many short-lived prefetch/resume tasks from a noisy neighboring tenant which drive IO latency and cause GPU attach delays. Expected behavior: Autoscaler should not shrink when there are inline IO-backpressure signals indicating transient congestion, and evictions should not cascade into a prefetch storm that amplifies tail latency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer workload: many short chat streams with long tail token generation (median 60 tokens, many short 1-5 token requests mixed).
2) Pool config: predictive autoscale enabled with cooldown 5m, reactive downscale threshold 0.35 active_slots for 3m window, kv-prefetch default, reserved GPUs: 16.
3) Traffic pattern: sudden shift from sustained medium concurrency to many ephemeral small streams (chatlets).
4) Observe allocator and autoscaler metrics across next 20 minutes: active_slots, attach_latency_ms, evictions_count, prefetch_io_ms, gpu_attach_failures.

Mar-10 11:07:20 autoscaler DEBUG predictive_estimate=9.8 reactive_window_mean=0.32 downscale_trigger=true

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Autoscaler misread low active_slots (caused by ephemeral short streams that sit idle between small token bursts) as sustained demand drop and initiated downscale.

Telemetry shows pre-downscale attach_latency_ms was rising (I/O tail) but the reactive metric window averaged below the downscale threshold. Predictive estimator had lower weight on short-stream variance.
After downscale, eviction induced many reconnections and prefetch re-warms from adjacent tenant I/O activity; scheduler shows concurrent prefetches peaking at 42 and nvme io wait rising sharply.
GPU allocation logs show attach failures increased x3 in the 60s after eviction and prefetched KV sizes grew by ~35% causing HBM pressure and spill-to-nvme leading to increased io wait.

No anomalous driver crashes; nvlink latencies normal. Root cause chain: (1) short-stream variance + estimator tuning -> premature downscale, (2) eviction-induced reconnections + noisy-tenant prefetch flood -> NVMe/io-congestion, (3) attach timeouts -> p99 tail spikes.
comments: Support (Aisha): Collected allocator/autoscaler traces and customer traffic sample; asking infra to hold on any permanent configuration changes until we validate mitigations.
SRE (Mei Chen): Noted similar signal pattern in SUP-712909 and SUP-403210; will instrument a transient 'io-aware' downscale inhibit for the affected window. Creating a canary on us-west-2 test shard.

Customer (SparrowAI - ops): We see client-side retries increasing during the spike window. Confirmed that traffic mix shifted due to an A/B rollout earlier that morning. We rolled it back at 11:15 and observed reduced tail.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): 1) Temporary change to autoscaler: add short-stream variance weight and an 'io-latency inhibit'—downscale suppressed when attach_latency_ms > 200ms for the last 90s. 2) Limit concurrent prefetches per tenant to 12 and throttle retries during attach backoff to reduce immediate reconnection fanout. 3) Customer rollback of A/B rollout reduced churn. Post-mitigation telemetry shows p99 reduced from ~1800ms to ~220ms within 12 minutes and eviction events stopped. Follow-ups: permanent autoscaler tuning and new telemetry dashboard tile for 'io-aware downscale signals', add a playbook entry in Confluence.
